record.original_question: Consider the same hard-core lattice-gas setting as in Conjecture 2.1, but restricted to non-regular trees with all fugacities equal. Can one prove the Conjecture 2.1 uniqueness claim in that tree setting?

evidence.quote: It seems to be an open problem to prove Conjecture 2.1 even when G is a non-regular tree and the w_x are all equal.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T=(V,E)$ be a countably infinite, locally finite tree (not assumed regular). Consider the hard-core lattice gas on $T$ with a common fugacity $w\ge 0$ at every vertex: a (finite-volume) Gibbs measure assigns to each independent set $I\subseteq V$ a weight proportional to $w^{|I|}$, where an independent set is a subset of vertices no two of which are adjacent. Infinite-volume Gibbs measures are defined as the usual DLR limits with hard-core nearest-neighbor exclusion.

For a rooted infinite tree $T$, let
$$\mathrm{br}(T)=\inf\bigl\{\lambda>0:\inf_{\Pi}\sum_{v\in\Pi}\lambda^{-|v|}=0\bigr\}$$
be its branching number, where the infimum is over all cutsets $\Pi$ separating the root from infinity and $|v|$ denotes graph distance from the root. For a real number $b\ge 1$, define the Kelly threshold
$$w_c(b)=\frac{b^{b}}{(b-1)^{b+1}}\qquad (w_c(1)=+\infty),$$
which equals the critical fugacity for uniqueness of the infinite-volume hard-core Gibbs measure on the infinite $b$-ary regular tree when $b$ is an integer $\ge 1$.

Conjecture: For every infinite, locally finite tree $T$ and every fugacity $w$ with $0\le w<w_c(\mathrm{br}(T))$, the hard-core lattice gas on $T$ with constant fugacity $w$ admits a unique infinite-volume Gibbs measure.

Prove or disprove this conjecture (uniqueness on arbitrary, possibly non-regular, infinite trees with all fugacities equal, in the entire regime below the Kelly threshold determined by the branching number).
artifact.status_search_result: There is substantial work on the hard-core model on regular trees (Kelly's threshold) and on bounded-degree graphs (Weitz, Sly, Peters–Regts, Brightwell–Winkler), but I could not locate a definitive result proving (or disproving) the uniqueness conjecture for the hard-core gas on general non-regular infinite trees with constant fugacity in the full subcritical regime governed by the branching number. The status appears to remain open or only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness thresholds on trees versus graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Brightwell–Winkler study uniqueness thresholds for the hard-core model on trees and bounded-degree graphs, indicating ongoing investigation of tree uniqueness questions.
status_evidence.claim: Tree uniqueness for hard-core model is a subject of continued research beyond the regular case.

status_evidence.title: Zero-Freeness of the Hard-Core Model with Bounded Connective Constant
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2026) work on zero-freeness of hard-core partition functions in terms of connective constant, building on Sokal's program.
status_evidence.claim: Sokal's conjectural program around hard-core uniqueness/zero-freeness continues to drive recent research.
